checks.result: All 1,542 source lines covered. No manuscript edits made.

Finite-site compact-resolvent assumptions and bounded interactions are stated before the general theorem. The abstract compresses these as finite-lattice scope. The gauge corollary explicitly supplies b_N in [0,2N], cubic plaquette incidence, fixed x=g^2, N>=2, unique gauge-invariant vacuum, and the excitation inequality. Claimed threshold 59.9 and 3x/16 lower bound agree textually. Fixed x versus fixed t Hooft coupling and lack of explicit-threshold infinite-volume construction are acknowledged.

The fixed-block result fixes m,p_B,N,x,b,a and varies only the exterior volume; proof states the ground-function ratio for all exterior configurations. Both abstract and introduction preserve fixed-block limitation and deny automatic whole-layer or coarse-operator persistence. Gauge commutation and possible zero physical discarded sector are explicit. The conditional scale budget is clearly hypothetical.

Finite-dimensional Schur statement and bounded graph-map closed-form extension have explicit domains and hypotheses. The multiscale result assumes exact metric-normalized reductions in common physical energy units and an actual terminal gap. The missing continuum construction, collective coercivity, generated-operator control and nontrivial finite-energy sector are explicitly listed. No continuum mass-gap or confinement theorem is claimed.

The paper credits BDL method and Yarotsky qualitative stability; it does not claim a new existence phenomenon, optimal constants, priority, global novelty or independent human review. Exact-source contents remain a separate literature obligation listed below.

Casimir, normalized Haar, magnetic coefficient, physical division by lattice spacing, vacuum subtraction, conditional projection and graph inner product are consistently specified. Reuse of C, K, M, n, P/Q, and s in different explicitly restarted contexts is local and not consequential symbol drift. No important globally missing definition was established.
